issue_context.title: win_domain_computer has no ability to check state
issue_context.body:
<!--- Verify first that your feature was not already discussed on GitHub -->
<!--- Complete *all* sections as described, this form is processed automatically -->

##### SUMMARY
win_domain_computer has no ability to check object state. There should be a state: check or something else to register if the object exists. Currently, you are forced to make an object or delete it. Excluding state defaults to present.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Idea

##### COMPONENT NAME
win_domain_computer

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
It would be very useful to register if a domain object exists or not to check that a process has in fact completed properly (vmware_guest domain join for instance).

<!--- HINT: You can also paste gist.github.com links for larger files -->
comments: win_domain_user has state: query for instance

cc @Daniel-Sanchez-Fabregas @ShachafGoldstein @if-meaton @jborean93 @jhawkesworth @nitzmahone
[click here for bot help](https://github.com/ansible/ansibullbot/blob/master/ISSUE_HELP.md)
<!--- boilerplate: notify --->

The fact that `win_domain_user` has a `state: query` option is not the way we want to move forward. To implement this feature we want to create a generic `win_domain_object_info` module that would work for all AD objects and return the attributes and whether it exists.

review_comments: Should add a point here saying not allowed with `I(identity)`. Should also say the value is the `C(distinguishedName) of the path to search from.`
I would also add to `identity`, `filter`, and `ldap_filter` some form of text saying one of the 3 must be set

```suggestion
short_description: retrieve info regarding domain objects of all kinds
```
Should add a point here saying not allowed with `I(identity)`

Although I think the `json_depth` option should be renamed as per my comment earlier.

```suggestion
    description: List of retrieved objects, each formatted at the maximum depth set by I(json_depth).
```
Due to this not being a valid parameter with `-Identity` we should remove the default

```suggestion
    filter: "sAMAccountName -like 'test*'"
```

This should use the proper LDAP attribute name for DN

```suggestion
      - This value is either the C(distinguishedName) or C(objectGUID) or the AD object to lookup.
```

```suggestion
    search_base: "OU=Users,DC=contoso,DC=com"
```
I believe the SearchBase is the `distinguishedName` of the path to search from, we should document that it is the DN
